transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Chen, thank you for coming in to see me today. I have something important to talk to you about. This is a difficult conversation to have, and I want to make sure we have plenty of time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is something wrong with the scan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. I have to tell you that we made a mistake with your imaging results from a few months ago. I am very sorry for this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: When the doctor looked at the pictures of your body, they saw a small spot that needed another look in three months. But that note was put in a part of the report that we did not see. Because of that, we didn't call you back, and the follow-up didn't happen. It is our fault that this was missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't... why?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a failure in how we read the report. We didn't look in the right section. I am the one responsible for your care, and I should have caught it. I am truly sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Was it... a bad spot?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you look worried. It is scary to hear that something was missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just waited. I thought everything was okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is very frustrating to find out you were waiting for a result that we already had.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Now what happens?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Here is exactly what we are going to do to fix this. First, I have already scheduled a new scan for you. It is for this Thursday at ten in the morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, this Thursday. I will personally call you on Friday afternoon to tell you the results. You won't have to wait for a letter or a portal message. I will speak with you directly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the spot? Is it gone?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't say if it is gone until we see the new picture. I don't want to give you a guess that might be wrong. But we are going to find out quickly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What if it is bad?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a heavy thing to worry about. If the spot is still there, we will bring in a specialist and we will meet again on Monday to map out every step of the treatment together. You will not be doing this alone.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't like the hospitals.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you've felt overwhelmed coming here. To make sure this never happens again, I have changed how we track these reports in our system. We now have a second person who double-checks every single section of the imaging report before we close a file.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You check it twice now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, twice. So no more notes are hidden in the wrong place.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday at ten.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. Do you have a way to get to the imaging center, or should I help you arrange a ride?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My son can bring me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That sounds like a good plan. Just to make sure I explained everything clearly, can you tell me what we missed and what is happening this Thursday?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You missed the note. The spot. Thursday is the new picture.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Exactly. I am sorry again that this happened, Mr. Chen. I know this is a lot to take in right now. We can just sit here for a moment if you need.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel... silly. Waiting.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are not silly. You trusted us to tell you if something was wrong, and we let you down. That is on us, not you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will give you a piece of paper now with the time and the address for Thursday. I'll write it in large letters.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will see you on Thursday, and I will call you Friday. Do you have any other questions for me right now?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. Just the ride.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Okay. I'll see you then.

H.justification: Resident allows patient to finish all turns, uses no rushing language, and offers to sit in silence with the patient.

E.justification: Error named in second turn, used lay language ('small spot'), checked comprehension via teach-back, and avoided false reassurance regarding the spot.

A.justification: Direct apologies used multiple times, explicitly taking personal and team responsibility ('It is our fault', 'I should have caught it') without deflection.

R.justification: Named specific emotions ('worried', 'scary', 'frustrating') and engaged with the patient's feelings of being 'silly' and 'overwhelmed'.

T.justification: Provided specific steps (scan Thursday 10am, call Friday), defined patient role (ride with son), and detailed the system change to prevent recurrence.
